Thanks for the details. Below is a 12-week progressive strength program designed to phase around her 28-day cycle, with special accommodations for days 1–3 of the cycle (flow days) when high-intensity work, heavy Valsalva lifting, and jumping are avoided. The plan assumes month-to-month timing starting 2026-06-01, with cycle days anchored to her 28-day cycle (Day 1 = onset of menses). If a cycle day falls on a non-training day, treat it as a standard recovery or light technical session as noted.

Assumptions and goals
- Primary goals: steady strength progression (squat, hinge, push, pull) while accommodating dysmenorrhea.
- Training days: 4 days/week (e.g., Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat) with optional accessory work on Sundays if energy allows.
- Throughout the cycle except days 1–3, keep intensity moderate-to-high with progressive overload.
- On cycle days 1–3 (flow days): no high-intensity work, no heavy Valsalva, no jumping. Use low-impact, low-load, high-control options and allow more rest.

Program structure overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and adaptation with cycle-aware load management. Build movement quality, establish baseline strength, and inoculate the body to higher loads outside flow days.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive overload with increased volume and intensity outside flow days. Introduce more structured strength blocks for the main lifts.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Peak strength and maintenance with deload around flow days, then final progressive overload to end of cycle. Emphasis on technique and stability.

Cycle-aware scheduling notes
- Flow days (cycle days 1–3): Focus on technique, mobility, activation, light loads, no heavy Valsalva, no jumps. If needed, swap a training day for an extra 1–2 rest days, but aim to maintain 4 days/week when possible.
- Non-flow days (cycle days 4–28, excluding the next menses onset): Normal training with escalating intensity and volume.
- The client’s cycle day mapping will be used weekly to adjust loads. If a period starts earlier or later, adjust that week’s plan accordingly but preserve the cycle-aware rules.

Weekly outline (for reference)
- Week 1–2: Foundation block with emphasis on squats, hip hinges, bench/push, pull, and core. Light to moderate loads with controlled tempo.
- Week 3–4: Increase sets/reps and introduce mild progressive overload; maintain flow-day accommodations.
- Week 5–6: Strength-building block; higher intensity on non-flow days; more challenging lower-body and upper-body work.
- Week 7–8: Volume and intensity peak for main lifts; incorporate accessory variations targeting weak points.
- Week 9–10: Deload/recovery week around flow days; rebuild with technique and light loading.
- Week 11–12: Final strength push with best-effort loads and a controlled deload to taper and consolidate gains.

Detailed plan

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 ( foundation and cycle-aware adaptation )
Weekly structure: 4 training days (A/B/C/D). Flow days adjusted.

Week 1 (Baseline and form emphasis)
- Day A (Lower: squats)
  - Back squat: 3–4 sets x 5 reps at 70–75% 1RM
  - Romanian deadlift (RDL): 3x8
  - Goblet squat or split squat: 3x8
  - Core: Plank 3x45s
- Day B (Upper Push/Pull)
  - Bench press or incline dumbbell press: 3–4x6–8
  - Barbell row or DB row: 3–4x6–8
  - Overhead press (DB or barbell): 3x8
  - Dips or push-ups: 3x8–12
  - Accessory: face pulls 3x12
- Day C (Lower hinge + 1-tempo)
  - Deadlift variation (sumo or conventional): 3–4x5
  - Hip thrust or glute bridge: 3x8–10
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3x8 per leg
  - Ab wheel or hanging leg raise: 3x8–10
- Day D (Active mobility & pulls)
  - Pull-ups or lat pull-downs: 3–4x6–8
  - Dumbbell Romanian deadlift: 3x8–10
  - Plyometrics avoided on flow days; if feeling good, light agility or step-ups: 3x10
  - Core circuit: 3 rounds (bird-dog, dead bug, Pallof press)

Note: If Day 1–3 of the cycle falls on any training day, reduce load by 10–20% and emphasize tempo (3–0–3–0) and control; avoid Valsalva, heavy loads, and jumps.

Weeks 2–4 progression
- Increase load by 2.5–5% for main lifts when form is solid and the bar moves smoothly.
- Maintain 4 days/week, but if flow days collide, substitute Day C with a posterior chain-focused light session or a mobility day.
- Accessory work: keep 2–3 supersets per session to enhance hypertrophy and stability.

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 (strength-building block)
Week 5
- Day A: Squat emphasis
  - Back squat: 4x5 at 75–80%
  - Front squat (or pause squats): 3x5
  - Romanian deadlift: 3x6
  - Core: suitcase carry 2x40m
- Day B: Push/pull
  - Bench press: 4x5
  - Bent-over rows: 4x6
  - Overhead press: 3x6
  - Pull-ups/lat: 3–4x6–8
- Day C: Lower hinge
  - Deadlift: 4x4–5 at 75–85%
  - Hip thrust: 3x8
  - Split squat: 3x8 per leg
  - Core: side planks 3x30s per side
- Day D: Upper/conditioning with mobility
  - Push-ups: 3x10–15
  - Cable row or DB row: 3x8–10
  - Lat pull-down: 3x8
  - Mobility and activation circuit: 15–20 minutes

Week 6
- Similar structure with +5–10% for main lifts where technically sound.
- Add small volume for accessory muscles: 2 sets of 8–12 reps for accessory movements.

Week 7
- Deload-like reps but maintain practice on form.
- Reduce volume by ~20% from Week 6, maintain intensity if comfortable, to prepare for peak weeks.

Week 8
- Return to higher intensity:
  - Back squat: 4x4 at 85% 1RM
  - Deadlift: 4x4 at 85% 1RM
  - Bench: 4x4 at 85% 1RM
  - Accessory: 2–3 exercises at 6–8 reps, moderate weight

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 (peak strength and cycle-aware maintenance)
Week 9
- Day A: Squat-focused
  - Back squat: 5x3 at 85–90%
  - Pause front squat: 3x3 at 80–85%
  - RDL: 3x6
- Day B: Push/pull with heavier loads
  - Bench press: 5x3 at 85–90%
  - Barbell row: 4x6
  - Overhead press: 3x5
  - Accessory pulls: 2x8
- Day C: Posterior chain
  - Deadlift: 4x3 at 90%
  - Hip thrust: 3x6
  - Reverse lunge: 3x8 per leg
- Day D: Mobility + controlled loading
  - Pull-aparts, face pulls, light rows: 3x12
  - Core: Pallof press 3x10
  - Mobility flow: 15 minutes

Week 10
- Maintain high intensity on non-flow days; reduce volume slightly if fatigue arises around flow days.
- Main lifts: 4–5x3 at 85–90%.
- Accessory: 2–3 exercises 6–8 reps.

Week 11
- Start taper toward culmination:
  - Squat: 3x3 at 85–90%
  - Deadlift: 3x3 at 85–90%
  - Bench: 3x3 at 85–90%
  - Accessory: 2–3 sets of 8–10 reps with lighter weights

Week 12 (Final push and deload)
- Week 12 should emphasize technique and recovery with:
  - Squat: 3x2 at 80–85%
  - Deadlift: 3x2 at 80–85%
  - Bench: 3x2 at 80–85%
  - Mobility and core: 15–20 minutes
- Finish with a closed-loop assessment: 1RM-ish checks for squat, deadlift, and bench if appropriate, or a submaximal 1–2RM test to gauge progress and plan future cycles.

Equipment and exercise substitutions
- If gym access changes, substitute with cable-based or DB equivalents.
- If a given lift is painful or technically problematic, swap for a safer alternative pattern:
  - For squat pain: box squats or goblet squats
  - For deadlift pain: rack pulls, hip thrusts, trap bar deadlifts
  - For bench pain: floor press or incline press
- Jumping or high-impact work avoided on flow days; on non-flow days, plyometrics can be reintroduced gradually (optional).

Recovery and monthly considerations
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours nightly.
- Nutrition: aim for a moderate protein intake (1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight/day). Ensure energy intake supports training; in higher-load weeks consider a slight caloric surplus if gains are not progressing.
- Hydration: maintain consistent hydration, especially around flow days if cramps are present.
- Menstrual symptoms management: consider heat therapy, gentle mobility, light cardio (walking, cycling) on flow days if tolerated. Gentle breathing techniques and mindfulness can help reduce perceived exertion.
- Recovery tools: foam rolling, mobility drills, and a 10–15 minute post-workout cool-down with static stretching and diaphragmatic breathing.

Progression tracking
- Track loads, reps, RPE, and subjective energy daily.
- If progress stalls for two consecutive weeks on a main lift, consider a microcycle deload or slight load reset (e.g., drop by 5–10% for 1–2 weeks while maintaining technique).
- Reassess 1RM or 3–4RM at the start of Phase 3 (Week 9) or after Week 8 to calibrate loads for Weeks 9–12.

Safety notes
- Emphasize proper breathing: inhale on the eccentric, exhale through the hard part; avoid Valsalva during flow days and when instructed.
- Focus on hips driving, bracing, and maintaining neutral spine on all lifts.
- If any unusual pain occurs, stop and reassess with form tweaks or medical guidance.
